cards.text: Judah has a new king, Amaziah, who's twenty-five years old and will reign in Jerusalem twenty-nine years. Twenty-five with a WHOLE kingdom? Friend, some days I can't handle one oven.

cards.question: Here's the Bible's verdict on King Amaziah: he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD. But there's a catch. What is it?

answers.text: He did it but not wholeheartedly
He did it only in his last years
He did it only when a prophet was near

cards.text: First order of business. As soon as the kingdom is firmly in his grasp, Amaziah executes the servants who murdered his father, the king.

cards.question: King Amaziah also puts to death the sons of the servants who murdered his father.
King Amaziah lets the murderers' sons live. What does he base that on?

answers.text: What is written in the Law of Moses
A promise he made to his mother

cards.text: Then Amaziah gets organized. He counts the men of Judah and Benjamin twenty and older, and finds 300,000 chosen men ready for spear and shield.

cards.question: King Amaziah has 300,000 soldiers, but he adds 100,000 more mighty men of valor. Where do they come from?

cards.text: The price for those troops: a hundred talents of silver. Friend, I went for a QUARTER out of a closing-down bin, and this king is dropping a hundred TALENTS on hired help.

cards.question: Then a man of God comes to King Amaziah with a message about those hired troops from Israel. What does he say?

answers.text: Don't let them go with you
Put them on the front line

cards.question: Why shouldn't Israel's army go into battle with King Amaziah?

answers.text: The LORD is not with Israel

cards.question: The man of God tells King Amaziah that if he fights bravely enough, he'll win even with Israel's troops along.

cards.text: Bravery won't save him, the man of God says, "for God has power to help and power to overthrow." And Amaziah's big question is about the money.

cards.question: King Amaziah already gave a hundred talents to the troops of Israel. What does the man of God tell him about it?

answers.text: The LORD is able to give you much more
The troops will pay it all back to you
That silver is gone so let it go

cards.text: So Amaziah sends the troops from Ephraim home. Now, friend, how do you think THAT news goes over?

cards.question: King Amaziah sends the hired troops from Ephraim home. How do they take it?

answers.text: They're sad to leave the king

cards.text: No hired help this time. Amaziah summons his strength and leads his troops to the Valley of Salt to fight the men of Seir, from Edom.

cards.question: Without the troops from Israel, King Amaziah loses the battle in the Valley of Salt.

cards.text: Amaziah strikes down 10,000 men of Seir. Judah's army captures 10,000 more alive, takes them to the top of a cliff and throws them down.

cards.question: While King Amaziah is off fighting, what do the furious troops he sent home do?

answers.text: They raid the cities of Judah
They join the army of Edom
They go home and stay quiet

cards.question: The dismissed troops raid Judah's cities but don't harm anyone.

cards.text: Now Amaziah comes home from beating the Edomites. And he does NOT come home empty-handed.

cards.question: What does King Amaziah bring home from the battle with Edom?
King Amaziah sets up Edom's gods as his own gods and bows before them.

cards.text: So the anger of the LORD burns against Amaziah. And He sends him a prophet.

cards.question: The prophet asks King Amaziah why he would seek Edom's gods. What's his point about those gods?

answers.text: They couldn't deliver their own people from him
They had already been broken in the battle
They were never worshiped in Jerusalem before

cards.text: The prophet's still talking when the king cuts him off: "Have we made you the counselor to the king? Stop! Why be struck down?"

cards.question: King Amaziah tells the prophet to stop or be struck down. What does the prophet do?

answers.text: He stops but gives one last word
He keeps preaching right through it
He walks out without a word

cards.question: The prophet's last word: God has determined to ___ Amaziah, because he did this and didn't heed the prophet's advice.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave Amaziah for now. Stick around, friend, because this king's story is NOT done.

findings.problem: The walkthrough says Amaziah spared the sons 'based on the Law of Moses', but it never says what that law says. The command in 25:4 that each person dies for his own sin is never told on any card. It is the heart of why he acted as he did, so the baker leaves without it.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The LORD is able to give you much more', is the only answer that sounds like Scripture or speaks of God. The wrong answers are everyday talk ('That silver is gone so let it go'). The right answer stands out by its tone alone.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'That silver is gone so let it go' is close to what the man of God means. He is telling Amaziah to dismiss the troops and not worry about the money. A baker could argue this answer is right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Up to this card, the troops have only been called 'from Israel'. Here they become 'the troops from Ephraim', and card 15 repeats this, without ever saying that the Ephraimites are those same Israelite troops (25:7). A baker could think these are a different group.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are

findings.problem: The raid in 25:13 is covered only by a true/false card that is easy to guess ('don't harm anyone'). No card ever tells that the troops struck down 3,000 people or carried off a great deal of plunder. Important details of the raid are missing.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The closing line copies the sample line from the doc almost word for word: 'And that's where we'll leave ... for now' followed by 'friend, this ... story's not done'. It is not a line written fresh for this passage.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The walkthrough has almost no humor. There are only two jokes, on stop 1 cards 1 and 8, and none at all in stop 2. Most story cards read as plain summary ('Then Amaziah gets organized.', 'So the anger of the LORD burns against Amaziah. And He sends him a prophet.'). Moments that could hold a real laugh go unused, such as bringing home gods that couldn't save their own people, or the king snapping at the prophet.

rule.text: But he is FUNNY. Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation.
